_doc: oilwatch pipeline v1 parameters. 'frozen' reproduces the frozen physics/attribution (PROJECT_CONTEXT.md, never changed). Every v3 value was fixed from literature/val BEFORE any v3 result was computed (E008 pre-registration, EXPERIMENT_LOG). Nothing here is tuned to Cerulean or to the official test set.

seed._merge_why: fragments whose gap <= 1 km form one slick event = Cerulean 500 m closing buffer (SkyTruth cerulean-cloud constants INFRA/DARK_CLOSING_BUFFER); fragment merging needed (KSAT: ~100 polygons/event, Bianchi et al. 2020)
seed._min_area_why: 64 px at the E005 x2 grid (17.8 x 19.9 m = 354 m2): E005 VAL misses 73% of GT components <= 64 px (EXPERIMENT_LOG E005), so smaller detections are below the detector's reliable size
seed._wind_why: C-band oil detectability window: ~2-3 m/s lower (look-alike regime below), ~10 m/s upper (Topouzelis 2008 Sensors 8:6642; Fingas & Brown 2018 Sensors 18:91)

physics_v3._doc: E008/E009-informed v3 ensemble. Forcing = SMOC uo+utide with SEPARATE Stokes (vsdx/vsdy), so windage must exclude wave drift: 0.02 + Stokes ~ 3.5% total (Roehrs et al. 2018 Ocean Sci 14:1581; OpenDrift default 0.02). Frozen 0.03/0.04 + Stokes likely double counts (E000 item 4).
physics_v3.model: OceanDrift transport-only (weathering irreversible; Breivik et al. 2012 BAKTRAK)
physics_v3._diffusivity_why: Okubo 1971 apparent diffusivity 0.2-3 m2/s at 6-48 h; MEDSLIK-II default 2, calibrated 2-13 m2/s (Accarino et al. 2025); OpenDrift example 10

backward_v3._doc: Density score with an age-dependent kernel: sigma(tau)^2 = sigma0^2 + (u_err*tau)^2. sigma0 covers slick geolocation + AIS + release offset; u_err = persistent current-model error (order of the frozen current-uncertainty range; centroid errors 2-3 km/day, de Aguiar et al. 2023). Ensemble spread is already in the particle cloud, so it is not added again.
backward_v3._persistence_why: ship-discharge slicks typically persist ~2-12 h (Liu B. et al. 2021; Cerulean temporal reference ~2.8 h): prior weight exp(-tau/12 h) on release age

forward_v3._doc: Forward hypothesis test (Longepe et al. 2015 MPB 101:826): each funnel vessel is assumed to discharge along its AIS track; the virtual slick is drifted to T0 and compared with the observed slick by the Fractions Skill Score (Simecek-Beatty & Lehr 2021 MPB).

geometry_v3._doc: Fresh-discharge evidence (Cerulean source scoring, SkyTruth cerulean-cloud scoring.py): head proximity P = exp(-(d/d_ref)^5), d_ref = max(3 km/h * dt, 0.5 km); heading alignment A = exp(-ln2*(dtheta/45deg)^2) (45 deg -> 0.5). Only meaningful for slicks younger than ~3 h (MAX_SLICK_DRIFT_TIME = 3).

age_v3._doc: Slick age evidence (no validated SAR-only age estimator exists; report an interval). Width diffusion t=((W/4)^2 - s0^2)/(2K) for K in the diffusivity range; Okubo 1971 sigma_rc^2[cm2]=0.0108 t[s]^2.34; forward best release window of consistent vessels; persistence prior.

fusion_v3._doc: Forward-backward averaging (Luo et al. 2024 MPB 207:116808): combined = sqrt(backward_rel * forward_rel), each normalised by the cluster maximum. Geometric mean penalises inconsistency in either direction. Tiers use absolute criteria so a weak field of candidates does not produce a 'strong' suspect.
fusion_v3._bwd_floor_why: exp(-2): at its best release age the vessel must lie within ~2 sigma(tau) of the drifted oil for backward support to count at all; relative rank alone can crown a vessel in a field with no real support. Fixed after the dev1 backward stage showed weak absolute densities, BEFORE any forward result existed.

forecast_v1._doc: Forward forecast T0 -> T0+72 h with weathering (OpenOil, NOAA weathering), GSHHG coastline stranding, v3 transport ensemble. Forcing covers to 2023-01-07 06:00 (T0+78 h).
forecast_v1._sst_why: ASSUMPTION: offshore northern Gulf of Mexico SST in early January ~21-23 C (NOAA climatology); no SST in the incident forcing. OpenOil default (10 C) would under-evaporate.
forecast_v1._m3_why: volume unknown from SAR; mass fractions (fate shares) are reported, not absolute volumes

sar_v1._doc: Tile-wise S1 GRD processing from the measurement TIFF (Microsoft Planetary Computer COG, no login). Heuristic thresholds, fixed before any SAR result.

darkness._why: no validated SAR-age formula; anchored on the Trujillo training oil damping median 6.36 dB (SAR_DATA_AUDIT s4) and 'strong/weak contrast' operator labels (Bianchi et al. 2020); descriptive only

ships._why: two-parameter CFAR (guard 11 px ~110 m > ship length, background 41 px); k=5 and +8 dB over clutter keep false alarms low on 10 m GRD; 4 px min removes speckle

match._why: moving ships are displaced along azimuth by ~R*v_r/V_sat (~110 m per m/s radial speed at R~850 km, V~7.5 km/s), so allow 1.5 km; stationary targets need no Doppler allowance
match._silent_why: vessel whose last AIS report is 30 min-3 h before T0 (none near T0); dead-reckoned from last SOG/COG; radius 1.5 km + 30% of dead-reckoned distance, capped at 3 km (cap added after the first run matched a 25 kn crew boat at 8-25 km: sanity fix, not tuned to any vessel)

twin_v1._doc: Twin experiments (oilwatch/twin.py). Fixed before any twin result. Truth physics deliberately outside the attribution ensemble; observation degraded like the real product.
twin_v1._buffer_why: E007 strands are 2-3x wider than the reference (E007 log)
twin_v1._shift_why: measured GCP/TPS geolocation median 39 m (E008 SAR stage)
twin_v1._fwd_why: 25 in the pipeline; 15 here to fit the laptop (fewer forward tests only lowers measured skill)

fusion_v31._doc: Absolute attribution rule calibrated on the calibration half of the twin experiments (max false accusation 10%), scored once on the held-out half. Applied beside the pre-registered v3 tiers.
